claim.text: Winning-ticket initializations discovered by iterative magnitude pruning on large, complex natural-image source datasets produce sparse initializations that, when used to train a VGG19 or ResNet50 architecture on other natural-image target datasets, frequently achieve test accuracies on the target tasks that are close to the accuracies obtained by winning tickets discovered directly on those target datasets.
The transferability described in claim 1 is observed across a wide range of pruning fractions.
Larger / more class-rich source datasets produced stronger cross-dataset transfer than smaller sources.
CIFAR-100 tickets generalize better than CIFAR-10 tickets despite both having 50,000 training examples.

Winning tickets discovered on larger source datasets—both in terms of number of training examples and number of output classes—transfer substantially better to other natural-image classification datasets than tickets discovered on smaller source datasets, for both VGG19 and ResNet50 architectures.

The effect described in claim 5, whereby winning tickets discovered on larger source datasets transfer substantially better to other natural-image classification datasets than tickets discovered on smaller source datasets, is not solely explained by raw training-set size.
Holding training-set size fixed, a source dataset with many classes produced tickets that generalized better across targets than one with few classes.
Winning-ticket initializations generated with one optimizer generalize to training with a different optimizer on natural-image classification datasets.
VGG19 tickets found using SGD with momentum or using Adam, when re-used with the alternate optimizer, achieve high performance that is comparable to tickets discovered under the target optimizer.
There are optimizer-dependent nuances in behavior in the transfer described in claim 8.
Tickets transferred from SGD to Adam sometimes under-perform random tickets at low pruning fractions but outperform random tickets at high pruning fractions.

A winning ticket discovered on CIFAR-10a (a subset of the CIFAR-10 dataset containing 25,000 training images with 2,500 images per class), transfers to a disjoint subset CIFAR-10b from the same data distribution and improves training on that held-out subset relative to random sparse initializations.
The within-distribution transfer described in claim 12 holds for both VGG19 and ResNet50.
ResNet50 showed sensitivity at low pruning fractions, occasionally under-performing random tickets when few weights are pruned.

When performing magnitude pruning for winning-ticket discovery on VGG19 trained on CIFAR-10, globally ranking weights across all layers and pruning the smallest-magnitude weights globally yields higher-performing sparse subnetworks than pruning a fixed fraction per layer.
Under global magnitude pruning the pruning fractions vary across layers: deeper convolutional layers are pruned more heavily while early layers retain a much larger fraction of their parameters.
For VGG19 trained on CIFAR-10, the structure of the pruning mask contains substantial information useful for training sparse networks.

Comparing (a) preserved winning-ticket masks, (b) masks permuted only within layers (local permutation), and (c) masks permuted across all layers (global permutation) shows that locally permuting a mask degrades performance moderately while globally permuting the mask degrades performance dramatically.
A fair "random ticket" baseline for evaluating a winning-ticket initialization should randomize both weight values and mask structure (global permutation).

For obtaining competitive winning tickets in the large-model and large-dataset regime of natural-image classification, an iterative magnitude-pruning schedule with pruning fraction per iteration 0.2 (20% of remaining parameters) over up to 30 iterations combined with late resetting to parameters at a small early training iteration—resetting to the parameters after 1 epoch for Fashion-MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and after 3 epochs for ImageNet and Places365—produced effective winning tickets, with learning-rate annealing schedules and other hyperparameters matched per model family.

Winning-ticket initializations discovered by iterative magnitude pruning on ImageNet, Places365, and, to a lesser extent, CIFAR-100 produce sparse initializations that, when used to train a VGG19 or ResNet50 architecture on SVHN, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, and Places365, frequently achieve test accuracies on the target tasks that are close to the accuracies obtained by winning tickets discovered directly on those target datasets.
The transferability described in claim 1 is observed across a wide range of pruning fractions, including very high sparsity.

Winning tickets discovered on larger source datasets—both in terms of number of training examples and number of output classes—transfer substantially better to SVHN, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, and Places365 than tickets discovered on smaller source datasets, for both VGG19 and ResNet50 architectures.
Holding training-set size fixed, CIFAR-100, a source dataset with 100 classes, produced tickets that generalized better across targets than CIFAR-10, a source dataset with 10 classes.

Under global magnitude pruning the pruning fractions vary across layers: deeper convolutional layers are pruned more heavily while the first convolutional layer retains a much larger fraction of its parameters.

note.text: elaboration of claim 20: Learning-rate annealing schedules and other hyperparameters were matched per model family
